data.title: Consolidated Zarr metadata across L1+L2 corpus
data.phase: L2 consolidated (11,573 shots) · L1 running on sun partition
data.summary: Run zarr.consolidate_metadata() once across the L1 and L2 corpora so every xarray.open_zarr() lands fast (~10ms) instead of falling back to a non-consolidated listing (10-100×slower). Eliminates the RuntimeWarning spam and removes a 0.5-2 s per-shot Zarr-open tax we saw on the failed signals job.

sections.body: Every ambix data audit / bulk-encode worker prints `RuntimeWarning: Failed to open Zarr store with consolidated metadata, but successfully read with non-consolidated metadata. This is typically much slower for opening a dataset.` On the 9,527-shot rbb corpus we already observed Zarr open dominating the per-shot wall time for the failed signals job (0% GPU util while CPU read the unconsolidated store). With 4 GPUs each fetching shots concurrently this becomes a real I/O bottleneck.

IMPORTANT: the FAIR-MAST corpus is **Zarr V3**, so consolidation writes a `consolidated_metadata` block into the root `zarr.json` (NOT a V2-style `.zmetadata` file). Verified on shot 11766: zarr.json grew to 605 KB with 351 consolidated entries. Subsequent `open_zarr(..., consolidated=True)` reads that one file instead of recursively listing every group/array over GPFS. Delivered as `scripts/consolidate_zarr_metadata.py` — idempotent CLI taking --root (repeatable) and --workers, run via SLURM (sun_debug for L2, sun for L1).

Script runs the open-time A/B internally (--measure flag): times xr.open_zarr on 3 representative shots per root before vs after. Results land in the per-run report JSON at /work/projects/imas_gpu/zarr-consolidate-l1-report-<jobid>.json. Target ≥ 10× open-time speed-up; confirm no RuntimeWarnings in the bulk-encode driver after.

Run via SLURM, NOT the login node (corrected mid-flight — see feedback memory). L2: 11,573/11,573 consolidated on sun_debug, 16 corrupt/partial shots failed (acceptable — same shots data-quality already excludes). L1: 17,111 shots running on the `sun` production partition (job 1207977, 36 cores, 3h cap, no debug walltime limit) — ~68 min expected. The debug partition's 1h cap was too tight for L1; production has no limit. Idempotent — safe to re-run when data-acquisition mirrors new shots.

followups.title: Run zarr.consolidate_metadata() across L1 + L2 corpora
followups.body: Single CPU-only run. Idempotent. Should finish in ~15 min and eliminate the RuntimeWarning we see on every Zarr open. Sets the table for the 4-GPU bulk-encode to be GPU-bound rather than I/O-bound.
followups.est_turn: single Sonnet turn · ~30 min dev + ~15 min run
followups.prompt:
Project: imas-ambix
Plan: zarr-consolidate (§2)
Tier: sonnet

Context
  Every ambix data audit / bulk-encode emits a Zarr non-consolidated-metadata RuntimeWarning and pays a ~0.5-2 s per-shot open cost. Run zarr.consolidate_metadata() once across both corpora so subsequent opens are O(10 ms).

Done-when
  1. scripts/consolidate_zarr_metadata.py committed — single-file CLI, idempotent, takes --root and --workers.
  2. Run completes for both /work/projects/imas_gpu/mast/level1/shots/ and .../level2/shots/.
  3. /work/projects/imas_gpu/mast/level{1,2}/shots/<shot>.zarr/.zmetadata files exist for every shot.
  4. Validation: time `xr.open_zarr(...)` on 3 representative shots before/after, log to plan §3.
  5. data.impl → 1.0, status → shipped; followup resolved with the speed-up numbers.
